10949-the-romance-of-zion-chapel-3d-ed.title: Zion Chapel
10949-the-romance-of-zion-chapel-3d-ed.creator: Richard Le Gallienne
10949-the-romance-of-zion-chapel-3d-ed.description: A book by Richard Le Gallienne. must console themselves with the gasometer. And indeed they seem more than content. For a street boasting the best view, as it runs out its sordid line longer than the rest, is proudly called Gasometer Street.

4837-history-of-the-united-netherlands-f.title: History Of The United Netherlands From The Death Of William
4837-history-of-the-united-netherlands-f.creator: John Lothrop Motley
4837-history-of-the-united-netherlands-f.description: A book by John Lothrop Motley. History has few so fruitful examples of the dangers which come from superstition and despotism, and the blessings which flow from the maintenance of religious and political freedom, as those afforded by the struggle between England and Holland on the one side, and Spain and Rome on the other, during the epoch which I have attempted to describe.

arxiv-2105-09928.title: Multi-Frequency Phase Retrieval for Antenna Measurements Thanks: Manuscript received December 27, 2019; revised May 25, 2020; accepted June 13, 2020; date of this version June 18, 2020. This work was supported by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy under Grant 50RK1923. (Corr
arxiv-2105-09928.creator: Josef Knapp, Student Member, IEEE, Alexander Paulus, Student Member, IEEE, Jonas Kornprobst
arxiv-2105-09928.description: Abstract Phase retrieval problems in antenna measurements arise when a reference phase cannot be provided to all measurement locations. Phase retrieval algorithms require sufficiently many independent measurement samples of the radiated fields to be successful. Larger amounts of independent data may improve the reconstruction of the phase information from magnitude-only measurements.

arxiv-2206-15114.title: The Learning by Confusion approach to identification of discontinuous phase transitions
arxiv-2206-15114.creator: Monika Richter–Laskowska, Marcin Kurpas, Maciej M. Maśka
arxiv-2206-15114.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Monika Richter–Laskowska, Marcin Kurpas, Maciej M. Maśka. Recently, the Learning by Confusion (LbC) approach has been proposed as a machine learning tool to determine the critical temperature T c T_{c} of phase transitions without any prior knowledge of its even approximate value. The method has been proven effective, but it has been used only for continuous phase transitions, where the confusion results only from deliberate incorrect labeling of the data.

arxiv-2211-15006.title: Fine-tuning language models to find agreement among humans with diverse preferences
arxiv-2211-15006.creator: Michiel A. Bakker, Martin J. Chadwick, Hannah R. Sheahan, Michael Henry Tessler, Lucy Campbell-Gillingham, Jan Balaguer, Nat McAleese, Amelia Glaese, John Aslanides, Matthew M. Botvinick, Christopher Summerfield
arxiv-2211-15006.description: Abstract Recent work in large language modeling (LLMs) has used fine-tuning to align outputs with the preferences of a prototypical user. This work assumes that human preferences are static and homogeneous across individuals, so that aligning to a a single “generic” user will confer more general alignment.

arxiv-2303-12700.title: ReorientDiff: Diffusion Model based Reorientation for Object Manipulation
arxiv-2303-12700.creator: Utkarsh A. Mishra, Yongxin Chen
arxiv-2303-12700.description: Abstract The ability to manipulate objects in desired configurations is a fundamental requirement for robots to complete various practical applications. While certain goals can be achieved by picking and placing the objects of interest directly, object reorientation is needed for precise placement in most of the tasks.

arxiv-2409-05569.title: DeepTV: A neural network approach for total variation minimization Thanks: Centre for Mathematical Sciences, Lund University, Box 118, 221 00 Lund, Sweden, andreas.langer@math.lth.se Thanks: Department of Biology, Lund University, Box 118, 221 00 Lund, Sweden
arxiv-2409-05569.creator: Andreas Langer, Sara Behnamian
arxiv-2409-05569.description: Abstract Neural network approaches have been demonstrated to work quite well to solve partial differential equations in practice. In this context approaches like physics-informed neural networks and the Deep Ritz method have become popular. In this paper, we propose a similar approach to solve an infinite-dimensional total variation minimization problem using neural networks.

arxiv-2412-05099.title: C/O ratios in self-gravitating protoplanetary discs with dust evolution
arxiv-2412-05099.creator: Tamara Molyarova, Eduard Vorobyov, Vitaly Akimkin
arxiv-2412-05099.description: Abstract Elemental abundances, particularly the C/O ratio, are seen as a way to connect the composition of planetary atmospheres with planet formation scenario and the disc chemical environment. We model the chemical composition of gas and ices in a self-gravitating disc on timescales of 0.

arxiv-2503-04583.title: Existence of Deadlock-Free Routing for Arbitrary Networks
arxiv-2503-04583.creator: Uri Mendlovic, Yossi Matias
arxiv-2503-04583.description: Abstract Given a network of routing nodes, represented as a directed graph, we prove the following necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of deadlock-free message routing: The directed graph must contain two edge-disjoint directed trees rooted at the same node, one tree directed into the root node and the other directed away from the root node.

arxiv-2505-14658.title: HDE-Array: Development and Validation of a New Dry Electrode Array Design to Acquire HD-sEMG for Hand Position Estimation Thanks: G. Rolandino, J. J. FitzGerald and B. Andrews are with the Nuffield Department of Surgical Sciences, University of Oxford, Oxford, OX3 9DU, UK (e-mail: giovanni.rolandino
arxiv-2505-14658.creator: Giovanni Rolandino, Chiara Zangrandi, Taian Vieira
arxiv-2505-14658.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Giovanni Rolandino, Chiara Zangrandi, Taian Vieira. This paper aims to introduce HDE-Array (High-Density Electrode Array), a novel dry electrode array for acquiring High-Density surface electromyography (HD-sEMG) for hand position estimation through RPC-Net (Recursive Prosthetic Control Network), a neural network defined in a previous study. We aim to demonstrate the hypothesis that the position estimates returned by RPC-Net using HD-sEMG signals acquired with HDE-Array are as accurate as those obtained from signals acquired with gel electrodes.

arxiv-2507-11163.title: Constraints on Kinetic Mixing of Dark Photons from Dilepton Spectra
arxiv-2507-11163.creator: A. W. Romero Jorge, E. Bratkovskaya, T. Song, L. Sagunski
arxiv-2507-11163.description: Abstract Dark photons, the hypothetical gauge bosons associated with an additional U ​ ( 1 ) ′ U(1)^{\prime} symmetry, can couple to Standard Model particles through a small kinetic mixing parameter ε \varepsilon with the ordinary photon. This mechanism provides a portal between the dark sector and visible matter.

arxiv-2606-07481.title: Drifting Models for Surrogate Flow Modeling
arxiv-2606-07481.creator: 1 Chris R. Jung † ; 1 Markus Dörr † ; 2 Natalie Jüngling; 2 Jennifer Niessner; 1 Adam T. Müller ‡ * {}^{{\ddagger}}\textsuperscript{*} ; 1 Nicolaj C. Stache ‡

europmc-pmc6302548.title: Dual Inhibition of the Lactate Transporters MCT1 and MCT4 Is Synthetic Lethal with Metformin due to NAD+ Depletion in Cancer Cells.
europmc-pmc6302548.creator: Benjamin D, Robay D, Hindupur SK, Pohlmann J, Colombi M, El-Shemerly MY, Maira SM, Moroni C, Lane HA, Hall MN.
europmc-pmc6302548.description: Highly glycolytic cancer cells prevent intracellular acidification by excreting the glycolytic end-products lactate and H + via the monocarboxylate transporters 1 (MCT1) and 4 (MCT4). We report that syrosingopine, an anti-hypertensive drug, is a dual MCT1 and MCT4 inhibitor...

pmc-10536217.title: Interface Engineering of CoFe-LDH Modified Ti: α-Fe2O3 Photoanode for Enhanced Photoelectrochemical Water Oxidation
pmc-10536217.creator: Yue Chang, Minmin Han, Yehui Ding, Huiyun Wei, Dawei Zhang, Hong Luo, Xiaogang Li, Xiongbo Yan, Hong Seok Kang
pmc-10536217.description: Effectively regulating and promoting the charge separation and transfer of photoanodes is a key and challenging aspect of photoelectrochemical (PEC) water oxidation. Herein, a Ti-doped hematite photoanode with a CoFe-LDH cocatalyst loaded on the surface was prepared through a series of processes, including hydrothermal treatment, annealing and electrodeposition. The prepared CoFe-LDH/Ti:α-Fe2O3 photoanode exhibited an outstanding photocurrent density of 3.

pmc-10627474.title: High throughput analysis of B cell dynamics and neutralizing antibody development during immunization with a novel clade C HIV-1 envelope
pmc-10627474.creator: Rohini Mopuri, Sarah Welbourn, Tysheena Charles, Pooja Ralli-Jain, David Rosales, Samantha Burton, Areeb Aftab, Kirti Karunakaran, Kathryn Pellegrini, William Kilembe, Etienne Karita, Sandrasegaram Gnanakaran, Amit A. Upadhyay, Steven E. Bosinger, Cynthia A. Derdeyn
pmc-10627474.description: A protective HIV-1 vaccine has been hampered by a limited understanding of how B cells acquire neutralizing activity. Our previous vaccines expressing two different HIV-1 envelopes elicited robust antigen specific serum IgG titers in 20 rhesus macaques; yet serum from only two animals neutralized the autologous virus.

pmc-10735773.title: PAIN ASSESSMENT AND MANAGEMENT FOR OLDER ADULTS WITH DEMENTIA IN LONG-TERM CARE: A SCOPING REVIEW
pmc-10735773.creator: Minhee Yang, Jeongwon Shin
pmc-10735773.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Self-reporting is essential for assessing pain. However, owing to their cognitive impairment, older adults with dementia may not always express pain. As such, older adults with dementia are at risk of living with undertreated pain. This scoping review aimed to explore and identify current publication trends and strategies regarding pain assessment and management for older adults with dementia in long-term care.

pmc-11500172.title: Research on X-ray security contraband identification technology based on lightweight YOLOv8
pmc-11500172.creator: Yaohui Fang, Chang Xu, Yulai Zhang
pmc-11500172.description: Aiming at the difficulty of identification and localization in the detection of contraband targets in X-ray images, as well as the demand for upgrading and deployment of security equipment during the peak flow stage, a lightweight X-ray security contraband detection algorithm is proposed and optimized for YOLOv8.

pmc-11548198.title: Brassinosteroids Alleviate Salt Stress by Enhancing Sugar and Glycine Betaine in Pepper (Capsicum annuum L.)
pmc-11548198.creator: Yujie Jin, Ping Yang, Jian Li, Yongchao Yang, Ruopeng Yang, Hongbo Fu, Jie Li, Vladimir V Kuznetsov
pmc-11548198.description: Salt stress is a major abiotic factor that negatively impacts the growth, performance, and secondary metabolite production in pepper (Capsicum annuum L.) plants. Brassinosteroids (BRs) play a crucial role in enhancing plant tolerance to abiotic stress, yet their potential in mitigating salt stress in pepper plants, particularly by promoting sugar and glycine betaine accumulation, remains underexplored.

pmc-11563940.title: Combinatorial lipidomics and proteomics underscore erythrocyte lipid membrane aberrations in the development of adverse cardio-cerebrovascular complications in maintenance hemodialysis patients
pmc-11563940.creator: Ke Zheng, Yujun Qian, Haiyun Wang, Dan Song, Hui You, Bo Hou, Fei Han, Yicheng Zhu, Feng Feng, Sin Man Lam, Guanghou Shui, Xuemei Li
pmc-11563940.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Patients on maintenance hemodialysis exhibit a notably higher risk of cardio-cerebrovascular complications that constitute the major cause of death. Preceding studies have reported conflicting associations between traditional lipid measures and clinical outcome in dialysis patients. In this prospective longitudinal study, we utilized quantitative lipidomics to elucidate, at molecular resolution, changes in lipidome profiles of erythrocyte and plasma samples collected from maintenance hemodialysis patients followed up for 86 months (≈7 years). Primary outcome was defined as cardiovascular-related deaths or new-onset cardio-cerebrovascular events.

pmc-11677720.title: The Loss of Tafazzin Transacetylase Activity Is Sufficient to Drive Testicular Infertility
pmc-11677720.creator: Paige L Snider, Elizabeth A Sierra Potchanant, Catalina Matias, Donna M Edwards, Jeffrey J Brault, Simon J Conway, Ioannis Georgiou, Cathryn Hogarth
pmc-11677720.description: Barth syndrome (BTHS) is a rare, infantile-onset, X-linked mitochondriopathy exhibiting a variable presentation of failure to thrive, growth insufficiency, skeletal myopathy, neutropenia, and heart anomalies due to mitochondrial dysfunction secondary to inherited TAFAZZIN transacetylase mutations. Although not reported in BTHS patients, male infertility is observed in several Tafazzin (Taz) mouse alleles and in a Drosophila mutant.

pmc-11693003.title: SOCIAL CONNECTIONS AND FALLS AMONG OLDER WOMEN WITH AND WITHOUT HIV IN THE UNITED STATE
pmc-11693003.creator: Lien Quach, Patricia Lloyd, Kristine M Erlandson, Tracey Wilson, Anna Rubtsova, Anjali Sharma, Jeffrey Burr, Mark Siedner
pmc-11693003.description: Falls affect one in four older adults annually and are linked to biological and environmental risk factors. Women with HIV (WWH) may be particularly vulnerable due to lower social support and higher loneliness but their relationship with falls is not well understood. We analyzed data from 1,068 women aged 50 and older in the 2017 Women’s Interagency HIV Study (WIHS).

pmc-11713404.title: Increased cerebral blood flow after lecanemab infusions: MR‐ASL utility in monitoring Alzheimer disease treatment response
pmc-11713404.creator: Anna S Nordvig, Andres Ricaurte Fajardo, Gloria Chiang
pmc-11713404.description: BackgroundSince lecanemab, an anti‐amyloid monoclonal antibody targeting Aβ protofibrils, only modestly impacts cognition (27% slower cognitive decline over 18 months), tracking the effects on the brain in the early months is a clinical challenge. Serial noncontrast MRI scans are required by the FDA, to assess for the occurrence of amyloid‐related imaging abnormalities (ARIA).

pmc-13056736.title: Designing for mild winters: evidence-based thermal comfort benchmarks from urban parks in a sub-tropical city
pmc-13056736.creator: Kevin Lau, Lingye Yao, Edward Ng
pmc-13056736.description: Outdoor thermal comfort in the cool season remains under-specified for humid subtropical cities. We conducted a winter field study across four urban parks in Hong Kong, collecting 611 paired questionnaire-microclimate records (December-March). On-site measurements (air temperature, globe temperature, humidity, wind) were linked at 60-s resolution to Cantonese surveys of thermal sensation.

pmc-13070659.title: Targeting delayed healing tissues: immune reprogramming of adaptive immune cells by biomaterials
pmc-13070659.creator: Zhiyun Wu, Fengzhen Meng, Yuming Xiang, Xiaohua Pan, William W Lu, Shaoquan Bian, Fan Pan, Liping Ouyang, Xiaoli Zhao
pmc-13070659.description: The adaptive immune system plays a pivotal role in coordinating tissue regeneration. Effective tissue repair and functional recovery depend on precisely regulating adaptive immune cells, especially T and B lymphocytes, and their dynamic crosstalk with innate immune cells. The immunomodulatory effects of biomaterials on adaptive cells could be realized through their influence on innate immune cells.

pmc-13083297.title: Tick–small mammal relationships in urban and forest environments in Yamagata Prefecture, Japan: First confirmation of the establishment of southern tick species in northern Japan
pmc-13083297.creator: Hirotaka Komine, Shinya Ishikawa
pmc-13083297.description: Small mammals are prominent hosts for ticks that transmit various infectious diseases to humans and other animals. Despite the widespread presence of ticks and small mammals worldwide and the fact that climate change is a global phenomenon, tick–small mammal relationships and the potential expansion of southern tick species have been investigated only in limited regions.

pmc-13146442.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A1405 THE BENEFICIAL EFFECT OF REPETITIVE TRANSCRANIAL CEREBELLAR MAGNETIC STIMULATION IN THE REHABILITATION OF POST-STROKE APHASIA: A RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED CLINICAL TRAIL
pmc-13146442.creator: Yang Liu, Yumei Zhang
pmc-13146442.description: Background and aimsAlthough studies have found that transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) targeting the right Broca mirror area can promote the recovery of language function in post-stroke aphasia (PSA) patients, this target has certain limitations, so the specific target has not been determined.

pmc-13240179.title: Universal Health Coverage and Health Equity in West Africa: Tracking Progress Toward SDG 3.8 in Ghana and Liberia
pmc-13240179.creator: Samuel Asamoah, Michael Sarfo, Olanrewaju Lawal, Sandra Konadu Bonnah, Michael Snowden, Jamie P Halsall, Godness Kye Biney, Angwach Abrham Asnake
pmc-13240179.description: BackgroundAchieving universal health coverage (UHC) remains a key priority for many low‐ and middle‐income countries, yet equity in access continues to be a significant challenge. This study examines the level and distribution of health service coverage in Ghana and Liberia, with a particular focus on wealth‐ and residence‐based disparities, to assess progress toward UHC and Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 3.8.

pmc-13376528.title: Fetomaternal hemorrhage in monochorionic diamniotic twins at 37+ weeks’ gestation: A rare complication
pmc-13376528.creator: Wei Zeng, Yaluan Bao, Yi Bin Ruan, Lizhuo Huang, Wan Ying Zheng, Yun Feng Lin, Huafang Lan
pmc-13376528.description: Fetomaternal hemorrhage refers to a clinical syndrome in which fetal blood enters the maternal circulation through the placental villous spaces, typically triggered by specific stimuli, and may lead to fetal anemia or maternal hemolysis. The occurrence of fetomaternal hemorrhage is very rare in singleton pregnancies and even rarer in multiple gestations.

pmc-13449549.title: Senkyunolide I Inhibits mtDNA‐cGAS‐STING Signaling in Macrophages via Targeting VDAC1 Oligomerization to Attenuate Ulcerative Colitis
pmc-13449549.creator: Zhiming Ye, Yihang Huang, Bohao Han, Lei Zhang, Can Yu, Yang Yang, Bing Liu, Yongping Jian, Zhixiang Xu, Cheng Zeng
pmc-13449549.description: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic inflammatory bowel disease with limited therapeutic options. The cyclic GMP‐AMP synthase (cGAS)‐stimulator of interferon genes (STING) pathway, activated by cytosolic mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA), has been increasingly implicated in UC. Through proteomics and artificial intelligence modeling, this study identified for the first time that senkyunolide I (SEI), a primary bioactive phthalide from Ligusticum striatum DC.

pmc-13570616.title: Investigation of the Research Competence of Applicants Enrolling into Doctoral Programs in Healthcare Professions: A Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-13570616.creator: Vitaliy Koikov, Gulmira Derbissalina, Ayagoz Umbetzhanova, Laura Kassym, Natalya Zemlyanskaya, Gulzhan Alibekova
pmc-13570616.description: PurposeSuccessful doctoral training requires well-developed research competence; however, evidence regarding the preparedness of prospective applicants to doctoral programmes in healthcare professions remains limited. This study aimed to assess research competence among prospective applicants to doctoral programmes in healthcare professions in Kazakhstan.Patients and MethodsA nationwide multicentre cross-sectional study was conducted among prospective applicants to doctoral programmes in healthcare professions in Kazakhstan.
